scope.purpose: Retained F1 admission-publication class inventory for the designated validation phase.
scope.approved_boundary: Publish one machine-wide admitted fact and generated_epoch; consuming readers own per-task eligibility, filtering before ranking and joining their task lists. Do not add task identity or per-task eligibility to fm-capacity-lib.sh.

finding.invariant: Every affected call path and compatibility axis must have an executable regression or an inspected unaffected reason in the retained validation handoff.
finding.cause: The changed publication contract had no retained class inventory; the generated handoff instruction alone supplied no inspection evidence.
finding.resolution: Record the shared serialization boundary, sibling consumers, compatibility axes and evidence gaps here without changing runtime admission or expanding the approved scope.

capacity.oracle: The approved machine-wide contract admits readable facts with reason ok and a free lane; unreadable facts refuse. Worked fixtures declare five lanes, four holders and 4 GiB available against a 3 GiB reserve, then replace the memory reading with malformed data.
capacity.rejects: Publishing admitted=false for the admitting fixture, admitted=true for unreadable input, retaining an old good publication on failure, or placing a full or stale machine.
capacity.limits: The explicit new admitted assertions cover successful and unreadable publication. Full, memory, pressure and disk refusals have existing behavioral cases, but not a new explicit admitted assertion for every refusal reason. The placement full fixture also changes reason and free_lanes, so it does not prove that placement consumes admitted.

call_paths.inspection: Both call fm_capacity_read then the sole fm_capacity_json serializer in bin/fm-capacity-lib.sh. Publication atomically saves the same facts it prints, including readable refusals and unreadable failures.

The ledger forwards remaining capacity arguments to fm-capacity.sh; activity selects its unchanged human report. Home-summary refresh invokes --publish best effort before replacing its separate summary document. None implements a second admitted formula.
call_paths.gap: The capacity suite executes ledger JSON and activity. Ledger argument forwarding for --publish and refresh scheduling were inspected, not executed in this fix round.

call_paths.inspection: Placement filters schema, readable, reason, timestamp and consistent numeric capacity fields before sorting by free lanes, headroom and name. It does not read admitted; the added field preserves that existing consumer and is not a new placement gate.

Fresh and relaunch workers call fm_capacity_read directly, excluding their replacement record. Control relaunch paths delegate to fm-spawn.sh. Deferred retry reads free_lanes from the unchanged human first line. None consumes the new serialized admitted field or gains a new admission rule.
call_paths.gap: The suite checks direct and control relaunch refusal with an occupied seat. Deferred scheduling and released-copy control routing were inspected, not newly exercised here.

call_paths.inspection: These named per-task readers are not supplied as implementations in this worktree. The approved scope correction assigns their joins and ranking to the consuming reader; neither the serializer nor its new admitted field proves that integration exists.
call_paths.gap: Private reader source, task-list joins, transport freshness enforcement and end-to-end reader evidence are unavailable within the permitted checkout; no private-reader integration claim is made.

representations_and_transitions.inspection: fm_capacity_read initializes unreadable with zero free lanes and returns early on unreadable input. Readable resource refusals and full occupancy set a non-ok reason; only success reaches reason=ok. The shared serializer emits the Boolean for both JSON representations and generated_epoch as the observation timestamp.

classes: dead or missing with no work
representations_and_transitions.inspection: Existing fm_task_record_holds_seat in bin/fm-project-capacity-lib.sh owns occupancy. PR readiness alone does not free a seat; unknown observations retain it; stopped records require process evidence, while stopped released-copy sentinels free their seat. No lifecycle rule changed with serialization.

classes: failed publication replaces prior success with refusal
representations_and_transitions.inspection: The existing atomic publisher replaces a prior success with current failure facts. Placement accepts only timestamps no later than now and at most 300 seconds old; advice reserves no lane. Spawn rereads live facts rather than trusting a publication.
representations_and_transitions.gap: The suite exercises stale and unreadable publications; future-time rejection is inspected in fm-place.sh rather than newly tested here.

classes: external bot without a local record
task_kinds_and_homes.inspection: fm_capacity_read skips secondmate records, counts remaining kinds through the shared seat predicate across fm_local_firstmate_state_dirs, and resolves policy via fm_project_capacity_config_dir. Local walk markers do not exempt workers; external bots without records add no occupancy. Remote machines publish their own facts rather than becoming local occupancy.
task_kinds_and_homes.gap: Fixtures cover ships, scouts, secondmate exemption and local registered homes. Remote transport and private remote readers are not exercised.

harnesses.inspection: The supported-name surface is bin/fm-harness.sh. fm_capacity_json does not read a harness or vendor output; all listed harnesses receive the same added Boolean. Harness-dependent occupancy remains behind fm_backend_agent_state and fm_agent_process_classify, unchanged by this branch.
harnesses.gap: Controlled endpoint states and real non-harness processes prove the portable seat rules, not classification of every currently installed vendor release.

backends.inspection: FM_BACKEND_KNOWN and FM_BACKEND_SPAWN in bin/fm-backend.sh list these six backends. fm_task_record_holds_seat reads each record's backend, defaulting absent backend to tmux. Serialization has no backend branch; fm-spawn.sh applies shared machine admission before backend-specific allocation. codex-app is not a supported spawn backend and gains no path here.
backends.gap: This focused regression does not prove real endpoint behavior across all six backends. Existing backend verification remains authoritative for those unchanged boundaries.

platforms.inspection: The added jq serialization field has no platform branch. Existing capacity memory paths read cgroup ancestors or MemAvailable; the human host-probe path distinguishes Darwin and other systems. These paths are unchanged. WSL follows Linux; this Bash/proc-based change adds no native Windows support.
platforms.gap: Finite, unlimited, root and unreadable cgroups use controlled fixtures. No new macOS, WSL-specific or native Windows execution is claimed.

account_selection.inspection: fm_capacity_read and fm_capacity_json do not resolve accounts, credentials, models or quota profiles. They aggregate machine state and resources. Account selection and quota enforcement in dispatch and spawn retain their existing owners; a machine-wide admitted=true is not proof a task's chosen account is eligible.
account_selection.gap: No account login, credential routing or real provider quota was exercised for this additive field.

documentation.inspection: Both now describe one machine-wide fact and assign task-list joining, per-task eligibility and filtering before ranking to consuming readers. The help path renders the script header. The admitted field and existing behavioral assertions remain intact.

live_validation_handoff.owner: The outer executor's designated validation phase; this review phase does not run or control it.

guards.purpose: Refresh real installed harness detection and tmux liveness underlying occupancy.
Refresh real Herdr lifecycle state and stopped-agent evidence underlying occupancy; a dependency skip is not live proof.

live_validation_handoff.status: Listed for validation, not run by this review fix. No new vendor-dependent check was introduced.
live_validation_handoff.required_evidence: Before claiming fresh live proof, record the date, installed versions, exact commands, output, skips and remaining backend/platform/private-reader gaps in the verification record. Existing historical evidence is not a current run.
